notes: BeyondArena food_delivery_time (Purucker et al. 2026, Table B.1: IID regression), from Kaggle rajatkumar30/food-delivery-time: predict the minutes to deliver an order from the delivery person's age, previous rating and the distance between restaurant and delivery location (data card). formula: bitrate ~ duration + height + width + `frame rate` + codec + category + (1 | id)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: UCI 335 README: the first file lists fundamental characteristics of 1.6 million YouTube videos (id, duration, bitrate, video bitrate, height, width, frame rate, estimated frame rate, codec, category, url) for insight into user-generated video; no model is fitted on it. Each id appears once per rendition YouTube stores, so renditions repeat within a video, whose duration and category are constant. bitrate (total kbit/s) is the response a reader would model from the rendition's size, frame rate and codec; bitrate(video) and frame rate(est.) are alternate measures and url a link, ignored. Hand check #162: stands; bitrate varies within nearly all of the 25,433 videos with two or more renditions; no bitrate model is documented.

OpenML 44992 fps_benchmark: FPS of video games measured on computers characterized by CPU and GPU, the fpsbenchmark.com rows of Peeters et al. 2021. Data Foundry's record: a full grid of 19 CPUs, 27 GPUs, 24 games and 2 settings, every cell once; on max settings log FPS = game + CPU + GPU fits almost exactly, and BeyondArena's video_game_fps_prediction (Table B.1: grouped regression) holds out CPU and GPU pairs. Rendered as crossed random intercepts for CPU, GPU and game on log FPS with the setting fixed; the Cpu and Gpu specification columns are constant within their part and stay usable, GameResolution is constant. The record retires the table because its values look like a site formula rather than benchmark runs; no source calls it simulated. No mixed model published. Hand check #162: stands; Data Foundry's log-additive diagnostic informs the log scale, and the source leaves open whether the data are artificial.

No mixed model published; the paper's moving-average features are derived and not in the table. Hand check #162: stands; stator_yoke, the fourth temperature the authors' code models, files no row, since the object holds three models.

formula: correct ~ `Average_confidence(BORED)` + `Average_confidence(CONCENTRATING)` + `Average_confidence(CONFUSED)` + `Average_confidence(FRUSTRATED)` + attempt_count + hint_count + skill_id + problem_type + bottom_hint + ms_first_response + tutor_mode + position + type + overlap_time + first_action + (1 | school_id) + (1 | user_id)
notes: ASSISTments 2012-2013 school data with affect (the file inside the Kaggle copy): one row per problem log of a student in the online tutor. TableShift (Gardner et al. 2023, App. B.15; tableshift/datasets/assistments.py) predicts correct from the affect confidences and per-attempt features, keeping rows with correct 0 or 1 (partial credit dropped), and holds out schools (school_id its domain). Students (user_id) are nested in schools; problem_id, teacher_id and student_class_id are further units left unused. Data Foundry's record warns that attempt_count, hint_count, bottom_hint, first_action and ms_first_response describe the same attempt. skill_id and first_action are codes. No mixed model published. Hand check #162: correct holds 5,323 partial-credit scores (11 values between 0 and 1) among its 6,123,270 rows, so it is stored continuous; TableShift's binary task keeps the rows with 0 or 1, a subset.

Wagner's givrep.R on OSF dha2j, the code behind the handbook chapter's table of RelIntensity, RelPitch and ProminenceShift: modelintensity=lmer(rintensity~Context+(Context|participant)+(Context|item),data=data), rintensity being the maximum intensity of the adjective minus that of the noun. The script fits the node's full alternatives.csv (data.csv), of which this file is the course subset, with the level spelled "No Alternative"; hence medium. Hand check #162: stands; Context is context in the course file. givrep.R's centered intensity-by-order model with full slopes, fitted before modelintensity, files no row.

Wagner's givrep.R on OSF dha2j: modelpitch=lmer(rpitch~Context+(Context|participant)+(Context|item),data=data), rpitch there being the maximum pitch of the adjective minus that of the noun in Hz; an earlier fit rpitch~Context*order with full slopes fails to converge. Fitted on the node's full alternatives.csv, of which this file is the course subset; hence medium. Hand check #162: in the course file rpitch is 1200 log2 of the adjective's over the noun's maximum pitch, in cents, and Wagner's report fits the same structure on the difference in semitones.

formula: runtime ~ algorithm + stacks + tiers + stack.tier.ratio + container.density + empty.stack.pct + overstowing.stack.pct + overstowing.2cont.stack.pct + group.same.min + group.same.max + group.same.mean + group.same.stdev + top.good.min + top.good.max + top.good.mean + top.good.stdev + overstowage.pct + bflb + left.density + tier.weighted.groups + avg.l1.top.left.lg.group + cont.empty.grt.estack + pct.bottom.pct.on.top + (1 | instance_id)
notes: CPMP-2015 algorithm-selection scenario (OpenML 41700; ASlib, Tierney & Malitsky features, Tierney, Pacino & Voss algorithms): the runtime of four A* and IDA* variants (algorithm) on each container pre-marshalling instance (instance_id), with the instance's latent-feature-analysis features repeated on its rows. Data Foundry's record (cpmp_2015_...) calls for a split grouped by instance. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per instance with the algorithm and the instance features as fixed effects is the reader's proposal; runstatus (ok, timeout, memout) restates the runtime. RULE GAP: runtimes stop at the 3600 s cutoff on timeouts and memouts and span orders of magnitude down to zero, and the rules settle neither the censoring nor a log scale. Hand check #162: stands; four algorithm runs on each of the 527 instances; 582 of the 2,108 runs end in a timeout (211) or memout (371) at the 3600 s cutoff (ASlib's algorithm_runs.arff), so runtime is censored.

MIP-2016 algorithm-selection scenario (OpenML 43071; Bergdoll, Open Algorithm Challenge 2017): PAR10 runtimes of five MIP solvers (algorithm) on each solvable MIPLIB2010 instance (instance_id), from Mittelmann's 12-thread benchmarks, with the instance's EPM features repeated on its rows. Data Foundry's record (mip_2016_...) notes that algorithm selection needs a split grouped by instance. No mixed model is published; the random intercept per instance with the solver as fixed effect is the reader's proposal, and the instance features, too many for the instances, stay usable. RULE GAP: PAR10 scores a timeout as ten times the cutoff, so the response mixes runtimes with a penalty, and the rules settle neither that nor a log scale. Hand check #162: notes corrected: PAR10 is ASlib's PAR10 plus the instance's base feature cost on all 1,090 rows, so the 218 timeouts score 72,000 s plus that cost; the response is censored.
